subject: URGENT: SilverCliff - hit-rate & throughput collapse after model v6.1 upgrade
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@silvercliff.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>; support@redwood.com
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@silvercliff.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production outage: latency/error spike after model v6.1 roll (samples attached)

Marcus / Redwood Ops team,

We pushed the model package you recommended (v6.1 / profile: fast-int8-slim) at 08:30 PT this morning. Within ~15 minutes we saw a sharp degradation across three signals: 1) end-to-end p95 latency went from ~180ms to ~480ms, 2) throughput (requests/min) fell ~40% versus baseline despite similar QPS, and 3) answer hit-rate for our lookup+rank flow dropped ~18% (see examples). This is impacting our authorization path — retries are spiking and customers are seeing degraded decisions.

I attached a latency trace, request samples and a small set of model outputs (sample_responses_v6.1.json). You can see a few examples where the model returns overly terse or truncated context, causing the downstream reranker to misfire. Logs show KV cache miss rate rising sharply at the time of cutover.

We need an immediate mitigation plan: can Redwood either (A) rollback to the previous stable variant (v6.0-stable) for our production routing, or (B) apply a traffic-split to divert 100% back to v6.0 until a fix is validated? We are ready to accept a temporary throughput-cost delta for stability.

Please treat this as P1 for SilverCliff. We are also flagging account SLA impacts — we’ll escalate internally if this is not resolved quickly.

Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Reliability
SilverCliff Payments

Lena — thanks for the signal and the attachments. I’m escalating immediately. Priya, Grace — looping you in for technical and executive coordination.

Lena, we can initiate an emergency rollback to v6.0-stable now and cut traffic back within the next 10–15 minutes if you authorize it. Before we flip, two quick asks: 1) can you confirm whether you have session affinity enabled (sticky routing for KV cache) or if your calls use short-lived session ids? 2) can you grant a short-lived access link to the trace bundle so Priya’s team can iterate quickly?

If we don’t hear back inside 10m we’ll proceed with the rollback to v6.0-stable under the emergency fallback policy and notify you once done.

—Marcus

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@silvercliff.com>, support@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production outage: latency/error spike after model v6.1 roll (samples attached)

Summary (initial triage):
- Observed behavior: v6.1 with "fast-int8-slim" shows ~2.5x token-infer time on our benchmark nodes for median-long sequences used by SilverCliff. Combined with lower KV cache hit-rate this creates queuing and backpressure on request workers.
- Root signals: higher KV cache eviction on the serving hosts (TTL + cache-size interplay) and increased per-token CPU during decoding when the int8 kernels fall back to slower paths for certain attention shapes.
- Impact: p95 latency increase, effective throughput drop due to worker saturation, and some outputs are truncated or missing prefixes which reduces downstream hit-rate.

Immediate mitigation plan (recommended, low blast radius):
1) Rollback routing: shift 100% prod traffic for SilverCliff to v6.0-stable. This is reversible and should restore baseline within 10–20 minutes.
2) Short-term configuration: temporarily increase per-host KV cache size for SilverCliff tenant and enforce sticky session ids to recover hit-rate (if SilverCliff can enable affinity).
3) Hotfix path: we’ll run a targeted kernel-path repro on a representative shard (using the attached latency trace + sample_responses) to identify the attention shapes causing int8 fallback and patch the runtime kernels or pick an alternate quant profile (safe-int8-preserve) for v6.1.

Attachments: rollback runbook (steps to automate traffic flip and health-checks) — rollback_runbook_v6.0-to-v6.1.pdf; I included the minimal checklist below.

Rollback checklist (ops playbook):
- Verify v6.0-stable image healthy in canary pool (done)
- Set routing rule: 100% -> v6.0-stable for tenant=SilverCliff (estimate 2m to apply)
- Monitor p95 latency and KV hit-rate, escalate if no improvement in 15m
- If rolling back does not restore baseline, open emergency infra ticket to increase worker concurrency temporarily

I’ll kick off the routing flip as soon as Marcus gives the green light and Lena confirms affinity details.

—Priya
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com

[attachment: rollback_runbook_v6.0-to-v6.1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: CTO <cto@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@silvercliff.com>, support@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 20:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production outage: latency/error spike after model v6.1 roll (samples attached)

Quick executive summary for leadership:
- Customer: SilverCliff Payments (mid-market, high auth volume) — P1 impact reported after automated rollout to v6.1 (fast-int8-slim).
- Impact: p95 latency spike (~+300ms), throughput down ~40%, hit-rate drop ~18% causing authorization degradation.
- Action taken: Priya’s team proposes immediate rollback to v6.0-stable (low-risk). Marcus is cleared to proceed pending Lena confirmation of session affinity.
- Ask of leadership: approve emergency rollback and sign-off for temporary SLA credit if rollback takes >30m to restore baseline. Also request approval to prioritize kernel-path repro for v6.1 on the next sprint and allocate 1 SRE on-call for 48 hours post-rollback.

Marcus — please proceed with the rollback at your discretion. Priya — follow the runbook and report p95/KV hit-rate at +5 / +15 / +30 minutes. I will coordinate the exec communication and credit assessment.

Grace O'Connor
VP, Customer Operations | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
